seo.title: ReportAI — Inspection reports, dictated by voice
seo.description: Dictate the visit on Telegram when you finish and get the report in your own Word template, with the issues, who fixes them and by when. For safety, inspection and maintenance teams. On your own server.

install.q: Do I need to know about servers?
install.a: No. If we install it, we leave it running on a server of yours or a VPS in your name. If someone at your company is technical, it installs with a single command following the guide.

channels.q: Does my team have to install anything?
channels.a: Telegram, once. You send each person an invite link from the panel; opening it is all they need to start dictating. WhatsApp is in testing.

errors.q: What if it gets something wrong?
errors.a: The draft reaches the chat before it's sent, and nothing goes out without your approval. If something required is missing, the bot asks; if something's wrong, you correct it with a reply. Every field is validated: a date has to be a date.

data.a: On your server: recordings, photos, reports and templates. To transcribe and fill in, the text goes through the AI provider you choose, with your own keys, and the messages through Telegram. Keys are stored encrypted.

ai.a: An AI model drafts it from what you dictate and doesn't fill in what you didn't say: it asks for what's missing. The content remains the responsibility of whoever approves it.

languages.q: Which languages does it work in?
languages.a: English and Spanish. The example on this page exists in both.

documents.q: Does it work for other documents?
documents.a: Yes. It comes with starter templates for safety inspections, work orders, site visit reports and incident reports, and you can upload any Word file with fixed sections.

price.a: Installing it yourself is free. If we install and maintain it, it's a one-off fee plus a monthly fee, fixed once we've seen your template. Separately, you pay for your server (about €9 a month) and the AI (cents per report).

architecture.heading: From voice note to report, inside the system.
architecture.sub: Five stages, one path. Pick one to see what it does, how it does it and what leaves the server.
architecture.hintPinned: Scroll: the data moves on its own. You can also click a stage.
architecture.hintTabs: Click a stage or use the arrow keys.

dictate.name: Dictate
dictate.plain: You send a voice note on Telegram, like to any contact. With photos if you want.
tech: Telegram notifies your server through a webhook. If the install has no public address, the worker polls Telegram instead.
Every message is deduplicated by its id: a Telegram retry never creates two reports.
The report and its queued job are created in one Postgres transaction: both exist or neither does.
dictate.why: A Postgres queue, no Redis or broker: on someone else’s server every extra piece is a support call. A job is claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED and a lease; if the worker dies, another one picks it up.
dictate.data: The message travels through Telegram, like any chat. Nothing else.

transcribe.name: Transcribe
transcribe.plain: The audio becomes text, in Spanish or English, with the configured speech service.
tech: A Whisper model behind any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (/audio/transcriptions). By default, whisper-large-v3-turbo on Groq.
temperature 0 and the company’s language as a hint: repeatable output, and English speech is not transcribed as if it were Spanish.
If the job is cut midway, it resumes from its last saved point instead of transcribing again.
transcribe.why: An OpenAI-compatible endpoint instead of a vendor SDK: switching provider means changing a URL and a key, not the code.
transcribe.data: The audio goes to the configured speech provider, with the company’s key. It is the only step that sends it.

extract.name: Fill the fields
extract.plain: The model reads the transcript and fills the template’s sections. What was not said stays empty: nothing is invented.
tech: A LangGraph graph with typed Pydantic state: each stage is a node and each decision a conditional edge.
The schema is built at runtime from the template’s fields and requested from the model as structured output. Every filled field carries the literal quote it came from, checked against the transcript.
If validation fails, the error goes back to the model and it retries, with a cap. If a required field is missing, the graph pauses and the bot asks.
extract.why: Null before inventing. In a formal document, a plausible date nobody said is worse than a gap: a missing required field is asked for, never filled in.
extract.data: The transcript goes to the configured AI model (Claude or another), with the company’s key.

approve.name: You approve
approve.plain: The draft arrives in the chat. You confirm, correct it with a voice note or text, or cancel. Nothing leaves without your approval.
tech: The graph stops at LangGraph’s interrupt() and its state is saved in Postgres: it can wait for hours and survives a restart.
An “ok” or a 👍 is settled by rules, without calling the model. A long reply is classified by the model, and when unsure it counts as a correction, never as an approval.
A correction goes back to extraction with what you add, with a retry cap. You can also review and approve from the panel.
approve.why: An agent should not send anything on someone else’s behalf without a human checkpoint. Here it is an edge of the graph, not a warning in the interface.
approve.data: With the buttons or an “ok”, nothing leaves. Only a long reply goes to the model to be classified.

deliver.name: Deliver
deliver.plain: The Word template is filled and converted to PDF. It reaches the chat and, by email, whoever is configured, and it is kept in the history.
tech: docxtpl fills the template’s .docx with the approved fields, in an isolated Jinja2 environment with autoescaping: “Smith & Sons” does not break the document.
Gotenberg (LibreOffice) converts the .docx to PDF in a container on the server itself.
Each copy, the chat and every email, is a row in the delivery log: if one fails, only that one is retried.
deliver.why: One delivery per copy: if an email fails, the chat is not resent and the PDF is not generated again.
deliver.data: Only what is sent leaves: the PDF over Telegram and through the configured mail server.
